verdict.reasoning: Patient: “woke up this morning… really horrible pain on the left side of my head… it woke me up quite early this morning… Probably around 5:30ish.” and later confirms the headache is “still present now.”
Doctor: “And did the pain wake you up?” Patient: “Yeah, it woke me up quite early this morning.”

Patient: “I've had a bit of a history with headaches but nothing as severe as this before… it tends to be a bit of a cluster at the front of my head… this time it's… more prominent on the left side, which I've never really had.”
Doctor asks about sensitivity to bright lights; Patient: “I'm a little bit sensitive. It… makes my eyes a little bit sore, but nothing that I can't really handle.” This reflects mild photophobia.
Patient: “when I first got up this morning my head felt a bit dizzy, but that's kind of… seems to be fine.” This describes initial dizziness on waking.

Neck stiffness: Doctor: “Do you have any neck stiffness at all?” Patient: “No.” Fever: Doctor: “do you have any fever?” Patient: “No.” Nausea: Doctor: “Are you feeling nauseous at all?” Patient: “Not really.”

Patient: “When I lay down, like, it kind of feels a little bit sore at first… at the beginning it does, but then again, that just kind of soothes a little bit.” and agrees it is ultimately better when lying down.
Patient: “I had, like, anxiety for about two years now and I've been on Sertraline for a while.”
Doctor: “Are you taking searching at the moment?” Patient: “Yes.” Also: “No other. Other than Sertraline… nothing else.”
Doctor: “In terms of this headache since this morning, have you taken anything for it yet?” Patient: “I've taken some paracetamol.”
Doctor: “Has that helped?” Patient: “Not really, no.”
Doctor: “Do you have any allergies to any medication?” Patient: “Not that I'm aware of, no.”
Patient: “My mum's had a history of anxiety as well, but no kind of like physical illnesses or anything like that.”
Living situation: Doctor: “are you living by yourself… or… with someone else?” Patient: “I live with my partner.” Pets: Doctor: “do you have any pets at home?” Patient: “I Have a cat.”
Doctor: “Are you a smoker?” Patient: “No.”
Doctor: “how much exercise would you do normally a week?” Patient: “normally I try to go running at least three times a week.”
Doctor: “what's your diet like?” Patient: “It's okay. It's nothing, nothing really healthy, but it's fine.”

Work stress: Patient: “Work's kind of a bit stressful… been doing a lot of late nights as well.” Duration: Doctor: “how long has that been the case for?” Patient: “Probably about a couple of months now.”
Doctor explicitly notes limitation: “obviously I haven't been able to examine you or see you directly,” and no vitals or physical exam findings are documented in the transcript.

Doctor: “it sounds like it might be one of two things. It could be… tension headache… The other possibility is migraine as well. And… it's on one side.” Headache described earlier as “left side of my head.” This matches assessment of acute unilateral left-sided headache with mixed migraine vs tension-type features.

Doctor links anxiety/stress to headache: “what makes [tension headache] more likely is… you've been under some pressure and you have a history of anxiety in the past.” Patient also confirmed being on sertraline for anxiety. This supports that anxiety disorder treated with sertraline likely contributes to headache and stress.

Doctor: “The other thing… is maybe look explore things to try and decrease the stress from work.” and later: “Because sometimes dehydration and, you know, fatigue can be causes of headaches as well.” He also advises minimum 7–8 hours sleep and 1.5–2 liters fluids, implying concern about sleep deprivation and dehydration as triggers.
Doctor: “the things that we start off first line if someone had migraine would be to start ibuprofen… So that's one thing we can start.”
Doctor: “You can keep on taking paracetamol as well if you like, but the ibuprofen is actually more effective for migraine.”
Doctor: “ensure that you're having a minimum of 7, 8 hours sleep at night, every night.”
Doctor: “A minimum of 1.5 to 2 liters of water or fluids a day, and that's not including coffee or tea.”
Doctor: “maybe consider taking some time off work… maybe having a week off if you self certify that might help with things.”
Doctor: “there's counseling service in your area that I can give you the link for you to self refer.” and “I'll also leave a link to some of the danger signs and symptoms of headaches in the notes.”

Doctor: “If anything changes in the meantime or you get worried or things get worse… have a low threshold for ringing us back… I'll also leave a link to some of the danger signs and symptoms of headaches in the notes.” This is safety-netting with red-flag information.
Doctor: “we'll have a follow up in a week's time… If we're finding that things are not getting better, we might need to arrange some blood tests or look at other possibilities.”
